newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ford dives to losses in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German Ford dives to losses in 1996.

text.p: Germany's Ford-Werke, a unit of U.S. Ford Motor Co, said on Tuesday it made a loss of 551.6 million marks in 1996 compared to a profit of 270.5 million marks in 1995.

Blaming the loss on one-off factors, increased production costs and shifts in its product range, Ford-Werke said the company had drawn up a plan that was aimed at putting it back in the black in 1997.
It said 1996 turnover had increased 5.5 percent to 26.4 billion marks.
German Ford said in a statement that it had sold a record 1.13 million vehicles in 1996, 7.2 percent up on the year before, giving it an 11.3 percent share of the growing German market.

Ford-Werke management board chairman William Boddie said the company would be seeking to reduce its costs in 1997 by three percent of turnover. He did not specify in the statement what measures would be used.
